name: Onychomancy

card.summary: Divination by reading fingernails, tied to palmistry; relevant to looks only through its focus on nail shape, length and decoration.
card.note: A fortune-telling practice, not a medical assessment; changes in nails can have medical causes worth discussing with a clinician.

quick.overview:
Onychomancy is a form of divination that reads the fingernails, often treated as a branch of palmistry. Readers look at marks, shape and length and interpret them for health, fortune, wealth and personality.

For appearance, its overlap is with nail care and styling: some systems tie longer nails to intuition, and the kikimancy variant reads the artificial nails a person chooses to wear.
quick.how: A reader examines their own or another person's nails, historically sometimes coated with oil in bright sunlight, then interprets markings using systems such as astrology, chakras, reflexology or tarot.
quick.risks: No physical risk from reading; relying on it for health judgments in place of medical advice is the main concern raised by commentators.

lead: Onychomancy, also called onymancy, is a divination practice that treats fingernails as a scrying surface. The word comes from Greek onychos, fingernail, and manteia, divination, and it is regarded as a subdivision of palmistry.[1]

In practice a reader looks at the nails of the person being read, sometimes oiled and held in bright sunlight, and interprets marks as signs for health, changes in fortune and personality. Medieval versions reportedly used the nails of a prepubescent boy.[1]

Interpretive systems vary: chakra systems assign each nail an energy centre and say longer nails improve intuition; astrological schemes link each finger to a planet, such as Mars for the thumb; reflexology and tarot systems assign body parts and cards to fingers.[1] The kikimancy variant links nail shape to the elements, yin and yang and personality types, and also considers the artificial nails a person wears.[1] Academics describe onychomancy as a pseudoscience, citing contradictory interpretations and no support for its predictions.[1]

chain: Reader examines nail shape, marks and length
Gives personality or fortune reading, with some systems favouring particular nail lengths or styles
angle.text: Onychomancy does not change how nails look; it attaches meanings to how they look. Its link to styling comes through kikimancy, which interprets the nail shapes and artificial nails people choose.

paras: The reader treats the nail like a crystal ball, interpreting symbols seen on it for health, fortune and character.[1]

Systems include chakra mappings, reflexology links between fingers and body parts, planetary assignments (thumb to Mars, index to Jupiter) and tarot cards for fingers, with broken nails read as reversed cards.[1]
Academic sources cited on the topic regard it as a pseudoscience because interpretations contradict one another and predictions lack support.[1]
